i_t_assibilation.description: A t-initial person-agreement marker surfaces as s after an i-final verb stem.
i_t_assibilation.source: Green & Morrison (2018), accepted manuscript pp. 23-24, explicitly gives kari+t+aa -> karisaa and describes t-assibilation after i. Puglielli & Cabdallah Cumar Mansuur (1997), Grammatica della lingua somala per le scuole medie superiori, pp. 97-98 of the grammar (PDF pp. 98-99), independently states that a t-initial ending after an i-final stem changes t to s and explicitly gives wey kari-s-ay (kari+t+ay) and waad joogi-s-ay (joogi+t+ay).

kari.class_evidence: Saeed (1999), Somali, uses kari as the Conjugation 2A example verb; Green & Morrison (2018) also treats kari as an i-final stem in its explicit assibilation example.
kari.development_evidence: Green & Morrison (2018) explicitly gives kari+t+aa -> karisaa. The runtime authorizes only the printed present -t-aa surface shared by 2sg and 3sg feminine; no kari past form or 2pl form is generated from this profile.

joogi.class_evidence: Puglielli & Cabdallah Cumar Mansuur (1997), section 6.3.2.1, describes the causative -in/-i extension and treats the i-final derived stem as the locus for Conjugation-II-style suffixal sound changes.
joogi.development_evidence: Puglielli & Cabdallah Cumar Mansuur (1997), PDF p. 99, explicitly prints waad joogi-s-ay and decomposes it as joogi+t+ay while stating that t changes to s when attached to the same kind of i-final stem. Only this printed 2sg past form is authorized.

benchmark_isolation.note: Runtime profiles are authorized from independent development sources, not frozen benchmark answers. Generation is finite, lemma-specific, tense-specific, and person-specific. Fayruus v9 remains evaluation-only.

notes: Finite Conjugation-2A morphophonology only. kari is present 2sg/3sg feminine; joogi is past 2sg only. The runtime does not infer other i-final lemmas, does not reverse-strip -saa/-say, does not fill unreviewed paradigm cells, and grants no correction authority.
